economic_intuition: High accruals predict lower future returns; the paper argues accruals predict returns because they are negatively correlated with the cash-based component of operating profitability.
detailed_definition: Accruals calculated using the Sloan balance-sheet approach, scaled by lagged total assets.

required_fields.concept: Book value of total assets used as lagged denominator
Delisting return, including paper-stated imputation for missing performance-related delistings
Market value of equity, required for sample and size sort
Book-to-market, required by sample and controls
SIC code used to exclude financial firms
Prior one-year return required by sample and controls

formula.paper_expression: Accruals = ΔACT − ΔCH − [ΔLCT − ΔDLC − ΔTXP] − DP; scaled by lagged total assets

evidence.quote: "Accruals is the change in current assets minus the change in cash"
evidence.interpretation: The Appendix provides the Compustat-variable formula and states all variables are scaled by lagged total assets.

evidence.location: Section 3 Data p.30; Section 4.2 p.36; Table 4 caption p.37
evidence.quote: "lag annual accounting information by six months"; "rebalance the portfolios annually at the end of June"
evidence.interpretation: This supports six-month accounting lag, June formation, annual rebalance, and July-to-June holding for portfolio sorts/factors.

evidence.quote: "missing values are replaced with zero values"; required sample fields are stated as "non-missing" in Section 3
evidence.interpretation: Required nonmissing sample fields are represented in universe.filters. This missing_policy records only the paper's zero-imputation rule for missing balance-sheet accounts used in accruals and CbOP calculations.

portfolio.universe: NYSE, Amex, and Nasdaq ordinary common shares matched between CRSP and Compustat, excluding financial firms.

evidence.location: Section 5 Cash-based operating profitability factor p.36; Table 5 caption p.38
evidence.quote: "first sort stocks by size into small and big"; "weak (below the 30th NYSE percentile) and robust (above the 70th NYSE percentile)"
evidence.interpretation: The paper explicitly uses NYSE breakpoints for a 2-by-3 independent sort to construct factor returns.

evidence.location: Section 5 Cash-based operating profitability factor p.36; Table 5 caption p.38
evidence.quote: "first sort stocks by size into small and big"; "weak (below the 30th NYSE percentile) and robust (above the 70th NYSE percentile)"
evidence.interpretation: The paper explicitly uses NYSE breakpoints for a 2-by-3 independent sort to construct factor returns.

implied_factor_direction.note: This is the paper-stated Table 5 six-portfolio factor direction.

comparison_policy.note: Compare Table 5 ACC in the paper-stated low-accruals-minus-high-accruals direction. The paper reverses robust/weak labels for accruals so the factor has a positive mean; do not compare to high-minus-low accrual decile returns without sign alignment.

adjustments.condition: missing delisting return and performance-related delisting
adjustments.description: If a delisting return is missing and the delisting is performance-related, impute -30%.

source.quote: "if a delisting return is missing and the delisting is performance-related, we impute a return of −30%"
source.interpretation: The paper specifies a -30% imputation rule for missing performance-related delisting returns.

source.quote: "We take monthly stock returns from ... CRSP"
source.interpretation: The factor is constructed from monthly CRSP returns with delisting-return treatment. Input-return components: ret_i,m: monthly stock return for firm i in month m; dlret_i,m: delisting return from CRSP when applicable

return_combination.note: Independent 2x3 sort: size split at NYSE median and signal split at NYSE 30th/70th percentiles. Middle signal portfolios are not included in the factor spread.

source.quote: "define each factor as the difference (1/2) × (small-robust + big-robust) − (1/2) × (small-weak + big-weak)"; "For the accruals factor the robust and weak labels are reversed."
source.interpretation: The paper states the six-portfolio factor formula and explicitly reverses robust/weak labels for the accruals factor, producing a low-accruals-minus-high-accruals factor.

portfolio_return.interpretation: The paper-original factor return is a value-weighted six-portfolio factor constructed from independent size and accruals sorts.

source.interpretation: This is the paper's main factor-return statistic for this paper-original factor.

source.quote: high-minus-low decile excess return -0.35% per month (t=-2.55)
source.interpretation: Table 4 is a portfolio-sort predictive-validity result, included as secondary evidence because Table 5 is the explicit factor construction.
